title: Inverse-image compatibility of the second scalar Ext tensor transport
statement:
Let k be a field, X,Y schemes, t:Y→X, and use the scalar sheaves, exact inverse image T, unit isomorphism u:T1_X≅1_Y and tensor functors of [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. Let δ_{M,N}:T(M⊗N)→TM⊗TN be the canonical oplax comparison, obtained by taking the mate of the direct image's lax tensor structure. For scalar sheaves A,B on X and A′,B′ on Y, morphisms φ:TA→A′ and ψ:TB→B′, q∈ℕ and b∈Ext^q(1_X,B), one has
$$T((\operatorname{tensorLeft} A)(b))\cdot\operatorname{Ext}^0(\delta_{A,B}\cdot(\phi\otimes\psi))=\operatorname{Ext}^0(\delta_{A,1_X}\cdot(\phi\otimes u))\cdot(\operatorname{tensorLeft} A') (\operatorname{Ext}^0(u^{-1})\cdot T(b)\cdot\operatorname{Ext}^0(\psi)).$$
All composites are in diagrammatic order and have degree q. No first Ext class is involved.

proof.text: For exact functors F,G and a natural transformation tau, prove Ext naturality by induction on the degree. In degree zero use mk0_bijective and ordinary naturality. For a positive degree embed the target into its injective object and use covariant_sequence_exact1 and eq_zero_of_injective to write the class as a smaller-degree class composed with the short exact sequence class. Map this composition by F and G, apply extClass_naturality to the short-complex morphism induced by tau, and use the induction hypothesis and associativity. Mathlib GrothendieckAxioms.Sheaf, ModuleCat.AB and GrothendieckCategory.EnoughInjectives supply enough injectives for scalar sheaves.

Specialize exactFunctorCompositionComparison with the identity natural isomorphism to identify mapping by a composite with successive mapping. Form the natural transformation from tensorLeft A followed by inverse image T to T followed by tensorLeft A-prime with components delta(A,M) followed by phi tensor identity. Its naturality is delta_natural_right and whisker_exchange. Apply the preceding Ext naturality to b.

Factor phi tensor psi into phi tensor identity followed by tensorLeft A-prime applied to psi. Rewrite degree-zero Ext composition and functorial transport, then use the naturality equality. Reassociate the right side until its adjacent degree-zero maps compose; tensorHom_comp_tensorHom and u.hom_inv_id cancel the unit maps. The resulting morphism is delta followed by phi tensor identity, giving the left side. This includes q=0, empty schemes and zero sheaves without extra assumptions.

theorem scalarExtCup_inverseImage_second (t : Y ⟶ X)
    (A B : KSheaf X k) (A' B' : KSheaf Y k)
    (φ : (scalarInverseImage t).obj A ⟶ A')
    (ψ : (scalarInverseImage t).obj B ⟶ B') (q : ℕ)
    (b : Abelian.Ext.{w + 1} (𝟙_ (KSheaf X k)) B q) :
    ((b.mapExactFunctor (tensorLeft A)).mapExactFunctor (scalarInverseImage t)).comp
      (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (((Opens.map t.base).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (ModuleCat.{w} k)
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)).leftAdjointOplaxMonoidal.δ
        A B ≫ (φ ⊗ₘ ψ))) (add_zero q) =
    (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (((Opens.map t.base).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (ModuleCat.{w} k)
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)).leftAdjointOplaxMonoidal.δ
      A (𝟙_ (KSheaf X k)) ≫ (φ ⊗ₘ (scalarInverseUnitIso t).hom))).comp
      ((((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (scalarInverseUnitIso t).inv).comp
        (b.mapExactFunctor (scalarInverseImage t)) (zero_add q)).comp
          (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ ψ) (add_zero q)).mapExactFunctor (tensorLeft A'))
            (zero_add q)
